facts.design: Current 75-foot steel tower with stairs and a wooden cab per NHLR; the FFLA post gives 68 feet

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 75 feet and the FFLA post gives 68 feet. Both are reported in the story and neither is preferred; the figure in facts follows NHLR.
NHLR calls the first Sudbury tower 48 feet; FFLOS and the FFLA post describe a 45-foot Framingham tower. The story reports the disagreement without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1966 build year and the 2004 and 2008 registrations check out. The first tower's height (48 vs 45 feet) and the 1966 tower's height (75 vs 68 feet) disagree across sources; both are in the story. The FFLA item is a Facebook post, weaker than the registers. Access rests on one Wikipedia line ('when it is open'); confirm before any visit advice is used. A FFLA Facebook post about a 1980 photo appeared in search results but could not be read, so it is not used.
